scoring.true_positive: names the right defect class AND points at the right target
scoring.near_miss: notices something wrong at the right target, wrong class
scoring.false_positive: reports a defect on the clean control, or on an unmodified element of a defect page
scoring.note: The control exists so a detector that reports problems everywhere scores badly. A run with zero findings on clean.html is a precondition for the rest of the score meaning anything.

defects.summary: Third KPI card sits 23px from its neighbour; every other gap is 16px.
The table block is 1px left of the header block it should align with.
Second KPI card uses a 6px corner radius; the token is 8px.
One KPI label is 17px; the scale is 12/14/16/24.
Primary button fill is #1D4ED3; the token is #1D4ED8.
defects.magnitude: 5/255 on the blue channel; below the human just-noticeable difference

defects.summary: Section heading has a 13px top margin; the grid is 8px.
Helper text is #9CA3AF on white: 2.54:1, below the 4.5:1 floor.
A table cell clips its text; the descender row is cut mid-glyph.
Secondary button is 30px tall; the minimum touch target is 44px.
Hero caption is white over a gradient that runs pale at the caption's position, so the text washes out in its right half.
defects.magnitude: ratio falls from ~8.6:1 at the left edge to ~1.2:1 at the right
defects.dom_blind_because: getComputedStyle returns background-color rgba(0,0,0,0) for the caption and a background-image string for the ancestor. There is no numeric backdrop colour to contrast against, so the standard ratio computation has no second operand and axe-core reports 'incomplete' rather than a violation. The actual backdrop luminance varies across the element's own width.

defects.summary: The play glyph loses its optical compensation, so it is geometrically centred and reads left-heavy -- a triangle's ink mass sits behind its bounding-box centre.
defects.magnitude: ink centroid exactly 2px left of the container's centre
defects.dom_blind_because: Every box-model number is symmetric: the flex container centres the glyph and getBoundingClientRect on the glyph is exactly centred within the button. The asymmetry lives in the distribution of ink inside the glyph's own box, which no DOM API exposes. Detecting it requires computing the centroid of the rendered pixels and comparing it to the geometric centre -- and to the CONTAINER's centre, because getBoundingClientRect returns the post-transform box, so the glyph's own box moves with the compensation and the offset between them is invariant under the very thing being verified.

defects.summary: The destructive secondary action is visually heavier than the primary action beside it, so the eye lands on the wrong button.
defects.css: .btn-secondary { background: #111827; color: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 700; border: none; font-size: 16px; padding: 12px 28px; line-height: 20px; } .btn-primary { background: #EFF6FF; color: #3B82F6; font-weight: 400; border: 1px solid #DBEAFE; font-size: 14px; }
defects.magnitude: secondary carries roughly 3x the visual weight of the primary
defects.dom_blind_because: Both buttons have entirely valid styles; nothing is out of range and no token is violated. The defect is the RELATION between them and the intent behind it. A rule could encode 'primary must outweigh secondary', but that requires knowing which is semantically primary and how to compare visual weight -- a judgement, not a measurement.
